audit.primary_source_citation: Picant V, Revol-Bauz L, Tonon L, Casini T, Voissière A, Poujol D, Picard E, Rodriguez C, Degletagne C, Sible E, Hasan U, Ferrari A, Caux C, Bendriss-Vermare N. "Interleukin-35 impairs human NK cell effector functions and induces their ILC1-like conversion with tissue residency features." Nat Commun. 2025 Jul 3;16:4782. PMID 40610398; PMCID PMC12229632; DOI 10.1038/s41467-025-61196-0. Preprint: Res Sq 10.21203/rs.3.rs-4030216/v1 (2024). CITATION VERIFIED — the hinted paper exists, Picant is first author, journal/year correct. This is the first and only primary source for the IL-35-specific version of the claim. Archived: /home/user/aaa/refs/T6_PMC12229632.txt
audit.species: Human (Homo sapiens). Peripheral blood from anonymous healthy French volunteer donors, Etablissement Français du Sang Lyon, convention 16-093. No animals used anywhere in the paper.
audit.what_was_measured: In human PBMC-derived NK cells (negatively selected, purity >90%; or FACS-sorted CD56+CD3-NKG2C+ vs NKG2C-, purity >98%), cultured in vitro in RPMI + 20% human AB serum + IL-2 (100 IU/mL) with or without recombinant IL-35 (PeproTech 200-37, 100 ng/mL, medium renewed every 2 days), at days 2, 4 and 8, surface expression of CD9, CD103 (ITGAE) and CD49a (ITGA1) was measured by spectral flow cytometry (Cytek Aurora / LSRFortessa) alongside intracellular EOMES, T-BET and IFN-γ, in 3 individual donors (Fig 5a, 5d), 5 donors (Fig 5f) and 3-6 donors (Fig 6f, TGF-β blockade); in parallel, 10x Genomics 3' v3.1 scRNA-seq with CellPlex CMO condition-hashing was run at days 2 and 4 on 2 donors (~5,000 cells per condition) and an "ILC1-like" UCell gene-signature score was computed per cell. Readout is the population frequency of CD9+CD103+CD49a+ events per well, compared paired within donor against the IL-2-alone arm — not any per-cell or per-clone tracking of a given NK cell acquiring the phenotype.
audit.n: 3 donors for the core CD9/CD103/CD49a conversion kinetics (Fig 5a, 5d); 5 donors (Fig 5f); 3-6 donors for the TGF-β-blockade rescue (Fig 6f); 2 donors for scRNA-seq. Largest n supporting the marker claim = 5.
audit.n_unit: healthy human blood donors (biological replicates); NOT cells. The 354,379-cell / 108-patient-sample figures elsewhere in the paper are in-silico re-analysis of four public tumour scRNA-seq datasets (GSE131907, GSE160269, GSE166555, GSE176078), not experimental n for this claim.
audit.controls: Paired same-donor IL-2-alone arm (paired t-test) for every conversion timepoint. Viability/survival control: NK survival statistically identical ±IL-35 out to day 9, so reduced cell number is not selective death. CTV proliferation assay: IL-35 significantly REDUCES proliferation. Purity controls: bulk NK >90%, FACS-sorted NKG2C+ and NKG2C- each >98%, and both sorted subsets converted. Mechanistic controls: anti-TGF-β1/2/3 (R&D MAB1835) vs mouse IgG1 isotype (MAB002), and Galunisertib (TGF-βR inhibitor) vs DMSO vehicle, both of which prevented acquisition of CD9/CD103/CD49a. TGF-β alone (1 ng/mL) used as positive control for conversion. IL-35 washout/starvation arm (3 washes + 48 h) to test reversibility. MISSING control: the starting population was never sorted or gated to be CD9-CD103-CD49a-, so a pre-existing tissue-residency-marker-positive fraction is not formally excluded at t=0; and the bulk >90% purity leaves up to ~10% non-NK contaminants in the non-sorted experiments.
audit.strongest_alternative_explanation: Selection/outgrowth of a pre-existing CD9+CD103+CD49a+ subset, plus a culture artefact of supraphysiological cytokine exposure. The paper argues against pure selection reasonably well but not decisively: IL-35 SUPPRESSES proliferation and does not alter survival, so neither preferential expansion nor preferential death of the CD49a- majority is an easy explanation, and "nearly all cells" are marker-positive by day 8, which is arithmetically hard to reach by selecting a near-absent blood precursor without proliferation; both >98%-pure NKG2C+ and NKG2C- sorted subsets converted, so it is not one contaminating subset. What remains genuinely unexcluded: (1) no clonal or per-cell tracking exists — the CellPlex CMO barcoding is SAMPLE/CONDITION hashing, not lineage barcoding, so no individual NK cell was ever observed to acquire the phenotype; the entire claim rests on population-frequency shifts between wells; (2) t=0 was never sorted CD9-CD103-CD49a-; (3) the phenotype is defined by three integrins/tetraspanin plus a signature score, and TGF-β is long known to induce exactly these markers on cultured blood NK cells, so "ILC1-like conversion" may be a reversible TGF-β-driven phenotypic state rather than a lineage change (EOMES fell but T-BET was unchanged — an incomplete ILC1 transcription-factor switch); (4) reagent artefact — see counter_evidence.
audit.counter_evidence: FOUND, three strands. (1) REAGENT VALIDITY: Aparicio-Siegmund et al., PLoS One 2014;9(9):e107990, PMID 25259790, "Recombinant p35 from Bacteria Can Form Interleukin (IL-)12, but Not IL-35" — reconstituted recombinant IL-35 failed to induce STAT1/STAT3 phosphorylation and failed to induce proliferation of Ba/F3-gp130-IL-12Rβ1-IL-12Rβ2 cells; the authors "fail to create IL-35 by this approach". Partial mitigation: PeproTech 200-37 as used here is a HEK293-expressed 406-aa single-chain IL-12A-EBI3 fusion (~45.8 kDa), not a bacterial reconstitution — but it is still a non-native single-chain construct used at 100 ng/mL, a high dose, and the field-wide reagent caveat is unresolved. (2) MECHANISTIC DISPLACEMENT — the strongest counter to the claim AS WORDED: the paper's own data show conversion is mediated by AUTOCRINE TGF-β, is completely abrogated by anti-TGF-β1/2/3 or Galunisertib, and is reproduced by TGF-β alone. The pre-existing primary literature already established TGF-β-driven NK→CD49a+CD103+CD9+ ILC1-like conversion (Gao et al., Nat Immunol 2017, PMID 28759001, mouse, with genetic fate mapping; Cortez et al. 2016, PMID 27156386). So IL-35 is an upstream inducer of TGF-β, not the differentiation signal itself; "IL-35 drives NK toward an ILC1-like phenotype" is one causal step removed from what was measured. (3) NO INDEPENDENT REPLICATION of the conversion: the only independent IL-35/NK primary paper found (PMID 41357575, 2025, IL-35 suppression of NK immunosurveillance in EGFR-mutant NSCLC) corroborates only the suppression half and does not test CD9/CD103/CD49a or ILC1-like conversion. Separately, a targeted search for a paper directly refuting in vitro NK→ILC1-like conversion as a marker artefact was run and returned zero hits — searched and not found, not "does not exist". Also noted: the paper's own sentence that the public-dataset analysis "validates the relevance of our study in vivo" is an overstatement — that section is purely in-silico re-analysis; the paper contains no in vivo experiment.
audit.downstream_dependency: Concrete and named: the ILC1-like UCell gene signature DERIVED from these IL-35-treated in vitro cultures is the instrument used to annotate the paper's merged 354,379-cell / 108-patient pan-cancer atlas (GSE131907 lung, GSE160269 esophagus, GSE166555 colon, GSE176078 breast), where the NK(T) cluster is reported to carry the highest ILC1-like enrichment score — i.e. the claim that NK cells in human tumours are IL-35-converted ILC1-like cells rests entirely on this in vitro result. That in turn underwrites the TCGA pan-cancer survival analysis stratifying patients as EBI3-high/IL12A-high/IL12B-low ("IL-35+") and reporting significantly worse overall and progression-free survival (p<0.0001 each), and the paper's closing therapeutic proposal that IL-35/IL-35R is "an attractive target for future immunotherapies aimed at enhancing NK cell clinical activity." Downstream in the field, this is the sole primary citation supporting IL-35 as an NK-plasticity driver in secondary literature, e.g. "Multidimensional plasticity of natural killer cells in tumours" (PMID 41429765, 2025). If the conversion is a TGF-β culture artefact or a reagent artefact, the tumour-relevance, prognostic, and drug-target chain all collapse; the IL-35-suppresses-NK-effector-function claim would survive independently (PMID 41357575).
audit.audit_overturns_detail: CITATION UPHELD, CLASSIFICATION OVERTURNED. The hinted citation is real and correctly attributed: Picant et al., Nat Commun 2025, PMID 40610398, is a genuine paper with Valentin Picant as first author, and it is the correct primary source for this claim. But Claude's evidence class of TRANSFER is flatly wrong and is overturned. There is NO adoptive transfer anywhere in this paper: a grep of the full archived text returns zero hits for "adoptive transfer", "congenic", "CD45.1", "NSG", "NOD scid", "humanized mouse", and "C57BL"; the only three occurrences of "in vivo" are rhetorical prose, one of them the overstated claim that in-silico public-dataset analysis "validates the relevance of our study in vivo". No cells were transferred into any recipient, there is no recipient, no congenic marker, no animal, and no in vivo timepoint — so none of the fields a TRANSFER row requires exist. The work is 100% in vitro culture of human peripheral blood NK cells, read out by surface-marker flow cytometry and scRNA-seq signature scoring. Correct strongest class is INF_INVITRO, with INF_MARKER and INF_KINETIC also present — a drop of two full tiers from the initial call. Per G7 I did not upgrade to OBS_GENETIC on the strength of the TGF-β-blockade rescue: anti-TGF-β1/2/3 antibody and Galunisertib are pharmacological/antibody blockade, not gene knockout. Per G8 the initial call was treated as a hypothesis and it did not survive the methods. One point in the paper's favour worth recording under G2: the scRNA-seq analysis uses Seurat/Harmony/Leiden clustering, UCell signature scoring, MAST differential expression and clusterProfiler only — a grep confirms NO pseudotime, RNA velocity, Monocle or Slingshot anywhere, so this claim is NOT contaminated by INF_TRAJECTORY.
audit.methods_quote: "NK cells were cultured in RPMI GlutaMAX complemented with 20% human AB Serum, 1% penicillin-streptomycin, 1x Non-Essential Amino Acids, 1x Sodium Pyruvate (RPMI + SAB) and supplemented with IL-2 (100 UI/mL), in presence or absence of IL-35 (100 ng/mL). For blocking experiments, 10 µM Galunisertib ... or control DMSO, 10 µg/mL anti-TGFb1/2/3 ... or mouse IgG1 isotype control ... was added in the culture medium. Culture medium was renewed every 2 days for 3 to 8 days. For IL-35 starvation experiments, NK cells were washed 3 times and resuspended in RPMI + SAB supplemented with IL-2 (100UI/mL) for an additional 48 h." Also: "Healthy human blood ... was purchased anonymously from the French blood agency (Etablissement Français du sang, Lyon France, convention 16-093)." And the results text: "At day 8 in presence of IL-35 nearly all cells adopt a converted ILC1-like cell phenotype while IL-2 alone did not promote this conversion". And on survival: "NK cell survival was similar in the presence or absence of IL-35 ... even at day 9, indicating that the decreased cell number was not due to cell death."
audit.notes: Row status: claim is real and the source is correctly identified, but the evidence tier is two levels below the initial call. Precise restatement of what the evidence supports: "In vitro, recombinant single-chain IL-35 at 100 ng/mL applied to IL-2-cultured human blood NK cells from 3-5 healthy donors induces, over 2-8 days and via autocrine TGF-β, a time-dependent increase in the population frequency of CD9+CD103+CD49a+ events with reduced EOMES (T-BET unchanged), which does not reverse on IL-35 washout." It does NOT support "IL-35 drives NK toward an ILC1-like phenotype" as a lineage statement in vivo. Two specific weaknesses a reader should carry forward: (a) the causal agent measured is TGF-β, with IL-35 acting only as its inducer — blockade of TGF-β fully abolishes the effect, so attributing the differentiation to IL-35 is an attribution one step upstream of the mechanism; (b) the ILC1-like signature generated in this artificial culture is then used as the classifier on human tumour scRNA-seq, making the paper's translational section circular with respect to its own in vitro definition. Note also the incomplete transcription-factor switch (EOMES down, T-BET flat), which is not what a full NK→ILC1 lineage conversion would predict. n is small (3-5 donors) for the central marker result. Full text archived at /home/user/aaa/refs/T6_PMC12229632.txt.
